name: ALTAI - Diversity, Non-discrimination and Fairness
description: Requirement 5 of the Assessment List for Trustworthy AI (ALTAI) by the EU High-Level Expert Group on AI

metadata.provider: EU High-Level Expert Group on AI
metadata.scientific_reference: High-Level Expert Group on Artificial Intelligence, Assessment List for Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence (ALTAI) for self-assessment, European Commission, July 2020, Requirement #5. Questions reproduced verbatim (typography normalised). Licence: reuse under Commission Decision 2011/833/EU (source acknowledged, meaning not distorted).

questions.text: Did you establish a strategy or a set of procedures to avoid creating or reinforcing unfair bias in the AI system, both regarding the use of input data as well as for the algorithm design?
Did you consider diversity and representativeness of end-users and/or subjects in the data?
Did you test for specific target groups or problematic use cases?
Did you research and use publicly available technical tools, that are state-of-the-art, to improve your understanding of the data, model and performance?

Did you assess and put in place processes to test and monitor for potential biases during the entire lifecycle of the AI system (e.g. biases due to possible limitations stemming from the composition of the used data sets (lack of diversity, non-representativeness))?
Where relevant, did you consider diversity and representativeness of end-users and/or subjects in the data?
Did you put in place educational and awareness initiatives to help AI designers and AI developers be more aware of the possible bias they can inject in designing and developing the AI system?
Did you ensure a mechanism that allows for the flagging of issues related to bias, discrimination or poor performance of the AI system?
Did you establish clear steps and ways of communicating on how and to whom such issues can be raised?
Did you identify the subjects that could potentially be (in)directly affected by the AI system, in addition to the (end-)users and/or subjects?
Is your definition of fairness commonly used and implemented in any phase of the process of setting up the AI system?
Did you consider other definitions of fairness before choosing this one?
Did you consult with the impacted communities about the correct definition of fairness, i.e. representatives of elderly persons or persons with disabilities?
Did you ensure a quantitative analysis or metrics to measure and test the applied definition of fairness?
Did you establish mechanisms to ensure fairness in your AI system?
Did you ensure that the AI system corresponds to the variety of preferences and abilities in society?
Did you assess whether the AI system's user interface is usable by those with special needs or disabilities or those at risk of exclusion?
Did you ensure that information about, and the AI system's user interface of, the AI system is accessible and usable also to users of assistive technologies (such as screen readers)?
Did you involve or consult with end-users or subjects in need for assistive technology during the planning and development phase of the AI system?
Did you ensure that Universal Design principles are taken into account during every step of the planning and development process, if applicable?
Did you take the impact of the AI system on the potential end-users and/or subjects into account?
Did you assess whether the team involved in building the AI system engaged with the possible target end-users and/or subjects?
Did you assess whether there could be groups who might be disproportionately affected by the outcomes of the AI system?
Did you assess the risk of the possible unfairness of the system onto the end-user's or subject's communities?
Did you consider a mechanism to include the participation of the widest range of possible stakeholders in the AI system's design and development?

name: FRAIA - Non-discrimination and Equal Treatment
description: Bias, discrimination and fundamental-rights questions of the Fundamental Rights and Algorithms Impact Assessment (FRAIA)

metadata.provider: Netherlands Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations
metadata.scientific_reference: J. Gerards, M.T. Schäfer, I. Muis, A. Vankan (Utrecht University), Fundamental Rights and Algorithms Impact Assessment (FRAIA), Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations, March 2022. Questions 1.5.1, 2A.3.1-2, 2B.3.4, 3.3.1-2, 3.5.2 and the Part 4 roadmap (4.1.1-4.7.1, to be answered for the right to equal treatment), verbatim (typography normalised). Licence: CC0 1.0 (government.nl copyright statement); the Dutch central government does not necessarily agree with the content of this checklist.

questions.text: Which parties and persons are involved in the development/use/maintenance of the algorithm?
What assumptions and biases are embedded in the data? How are their influences on the algorithm's output corrected or otherwise overcome or mitigated (see also annex 2)?
questions.category: Part 2A: What? (input) – 2A.3 Bias/assumptions in the data

questions.text: If training data is used: is the data representative for the context in which the algorithm will be used?
questions.category: Part 2A: What? (input) – 2A.3 Bias/assumptions in the data

questions.text: What measures can be taken to counteract the risks of reproduction or even amplification of biases (e.g. different sampling strategy, feature modification, ...)?
What will be the effects of using the algorithm for citizens and how will the 'human measure' be considered when making decisions based on the algorithm?
questions.category: Part 3: How? – 3.3 Effects of the algorithm

questions.text: What are the risks of stigmatisation, discrimination or otherwise harmful or adverse effects on citizens? How will these be combated or mitigated?
questions.category: Part 3: How? – 3.3 Effects of the algorithm

questions.text: Area: where will the algorithm be used? Is it in a specific geographical area; does the algorithm concern a certain group of persons or cases?
Is any fundamental right affected by the algorithm that is to be used?
Do specific legal provisions or standards apply to the fundamental rights infringement?
questions.category: Part 4: Fundamental rights – 4.2 Specific legislation and standards

questions.text: How seriously is a fundamental right affected by the algorithm?
Which objectives are pursued by using the algorithm?
Is the algorithm that is to be used a suitable means to realise the set objectives?
Is using this specific algorithm necessary to achieve this objective, and are there no other or mitigating measures available to do so?
questions.category: Part 4: Fundamental rights – 4.6 Necessity and subsidiarity

questions.text: Does the use of the algorithm result in a reasonable balance between the objectives pursued and the fundamental rights that will be infringed?

name: NIST AI RMF - Fairness and Bias
description: Transparency and documentation questions of the NIST AI RMF Playbook for GOVERN 3.1, MAP 1.2, MEASURE 2.2 and MEASURE 2.11

metadata.scientific_reference: NIST AI Risk Management Framework Playbook (companion to NIST AI 100-1), Transparency & Documentation items of GOVERN 3.1, MAP 1.2, MEASURE 2.2 and MEASURE 2.11, verbatim (typography normalised); questions repeated across these subcategories kept once. Licence: US Government work, not subject to copyright in the US (17 U.S.C. 105); some items adapt cited third-party sources.

questions.text: Are the relevant staff dealing with AI systems properly trained to interpret AI model output and decisions as well as to detect and manage bias in data?
questions.category: GOVERN 3.1 – Diverse team informs AI risk decisions

questions.text: Entities include diverse perspectives from technical and non-technical communities throughout the AI life cycle to anticipate and mitigate unintended consequences including potential bias and discrimination.
questions.category: GOVERN 3.1 – Diverse team informs AI risk decisions

questions.text: Stakeholder involvement: Include diverse perspectives from a community of stakeholders throughout the AI life cycle to mitigate risks.
questions.category: GOVERN 3.1 – Diverse team informs AI risk decisions

questions.text: Strategies to incorporate diverse perspectives include establishing collaborative processes and multidisciplinary teams that involve subject matter experts in data science, software development, civil liberties, privacy and security, legal counsel, and risk management.
questions.category: GOVERN 3.1 – Diverse team informs AI risk decisions

questions.text: To what extent are the established procedures effective in mitigating bias, inequity, and other concerns resulting from the system?
questions.category: GOVERN 3.1 – Diverse team informs AI risk decisions

questions.text: To what extent do the teams responsible for developing and maintaining the AI system reflect diverse opinions, backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives?
questions.category: MAP 1.2 – Demographically diverse, interdisciplinary AI actors

questions.text: Did the entity document the demographics of those involved in the design and development of the AI system to capture and communicate potential biases inherent to the development process, according to forum participants?
questions.category: MAP 1.2 – Demographically diverse, interdisciplinary AI actors

questions.text: What specific perspectives did stakeholders share, and how were they integrated across the design, development, deployment, assessment, and monitoring of the AI system?
questions.category: MAP 1.2 – Demographically diverse, interdisciplinary AI actors

questions.text: To what extent has the entity addressed stakeholder perspectives on the potential negative impacts of the AI system on end users and impacted populations?
questions.category: MAP 1.2 – Demographically diverse, interdisciplinary AI actors

questions.text: What type of information is accessible on the design, operations, and limitations of the AI system to external stakeholders, including end users, consumers, regulators, and individuals impacted by use of the AI system?
questions.category: MAP 1.2 – Demographically diverse, interdisciplinary AI actors

questions.text: Did your organization address usability problems and test whether user interfaces served their intended purposes? Consulting the community or end users at the earliest stages of development to ensure there is transparency on the technology used and how it is deployed.
questions.category: MAP 1.2 – Demographically diverse, interdisciplinary AI actors

questions.text: Given the purpose of this AI, what is an appropriate interval for checking whether it is still accurate, unbiased, explainable, etc.? What are the checks for this model?
questions.category: MEASURE 2.2 – Human-subject evaluations representative of the population

questions.text: How has the entity identified and mitigated potential impacts of bias in the data, including inequitable or discriminatory outcomes?
questions.category: MEASURE 2.2 – Human-subject evaluations representative of the population

questions.text: To what extent has the entity identified and mitigated potential bias—statistical, contextual, and historical—in the data?
questions.category: MEASURE 2.2 – Human-subject evaluations representative of the population

questions.text: If it relates to people, were they told what the dataset would be used for and did they consent? What community norms exist for data collected from human communications? If consent was obtained, how? Were the people provided with any mechanism to revoke their consent in the future or for certain uses?
questions.category: MEASURE 2.2 – Human-subject evaluations representative of the population

questions.text: If human subjects were used in the development or testing of the AI system, what protections were put in place to promote their safety and wellbeing?
questions.category: MEASURE 2.2 – Human-subject evaluations representative of the population

questions.text: If it relates to people, does it unfairly advantage or disadvantage a particular social group? In what ways? How was this mitigated?
Were adversarial machine learning approaches considered or used for measuring bias (e.g.: prompt engineering, adversarial models)

name: AI Verify - Fairness Process Checks
description: Fairness process checks 7.1.1-7.9.1 of the AI Verify testing framework

metadata.scientific_reference:
AI Verify Foundation, AI Verify process checklist, Fairness principle (checks 7.1.1-7.9.1), aiverify-foundation/aiverify@3f58c3e, verbatim (typography normalised) (line breaks in place of
). Licence: Apache License 2.0.

questions.text: Apply counterfactual fairness assessment
questions.category: Assess within-group fairness (also known as individual fairness)

questions.text: Monitor the changes in fairness metric values in the lifecycle of the AI system.
questions.category: Put in place processes to test for potential biases during the entire lifecycle of the AI system, so that practitioners can act to mitigate biases based on feedback (e.g., biases due to possible limitations stemming from the composition of the used data sets such as a lack of diversity and non-representativeness)

questions.text: Consider using Fairness Decision Tree (e.g., AI Verify, Aequitas) to select the appropriate metric(s) for your application
questions.category: Establish a strategy for the selection of fairness metrics that are aligned with the desired outcomes of the AI system's intended application

questions.text: Identify the sensitive features and their privileged and unprivileged groups where feasible.
questions.category: Define sensitive features for the organisation that are consistent with the legislation and corporate values

questions.text: Where feasible, consult the impacted communities on the correct definition of fairness (e.g., representatives of elderly persons or persons with disabilities), values and considerations of those impacted (e.g., individual's preference)
questions.category: Define sensitive features for the organisation that are consistent with the legislation and corporate values

questions.text: Define this partitioning in terms of sensitive features that models should be prohibited from being trained on, but are used in the evaluation of fairness outcomes.
questions.category: Establish a process for identifying and selecting sub-populations between which the AI system should produce fair outcomes

questions.text: Perform exploratory data analysis. For the sensitive feature, test the representation of each group in the data. Resample data or collect more data if a particular group is severely underrepresented.
questions.category: Establish a strategy or a set of procedures to check that the data used in the training of the AI model, is representative of the population who make up the end-users of the AI model

questions.text: Monitor threshold violations of fairness metrics post-deployment and for actual harms
questions.category: Put in place a mechanism that allows for the flagging of issues related to bias, discrimination, or poor performance of the AI system

questions.text: Monitor metrics for the latest set of data for the model currently being deployed on an ongoing basis.
questions.category: Put in place appropriate mechanisms to ensure fairness in your AI system

questions.text:
Where possible, handle imbalanced training sets with minorities. Examples:
- Oversample minority class
- Undersample majority class
- Generate synthetic samples (SMOTE)
questions.category: Address the risk of biases due to possible limitations stemming from the composition of the used data sets (lack of diversity, non-representativeness), by applying appropriate adjustments on data samples of minorities
